content.overview: Section 2 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 defines key terms used throughout the Act, including access, addressee, computer, computer network, computer resource, computer system, data, digital signature, electronic form, electronic record, information, intermediary, originator and secure system. Correct application of civil and criminal provisions depends on these definitions. Always read definitions against the official text as in force.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Which defined term is in issue? (2) Does the fact pattern match computer resource / electronic record / intermediary? (3) How does the definition feed ss. 43/65–67 analysis?
content.study:
Definitions control the reach of duties and offences. Do not expand computer resource beyond the enacted meaning without the text.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Function of s. 2
sections.body: Supplies statutory meanings for computer, computer resource, electronic record, digital signature, intermediary, data and related terms.

sections.heading: Computer resource
sections.body: Includes computer, computer system, computer network, data, computer database or software — as defined; central to ss. 43 and 66 analysis.

sections.heading: Electronic record / digital signature
sections.body: Electronic record is data, record or data generated, image or sound stored, received or sent in an electronic form; digital signature is authentication by electronic method as defined.

sections.heading: Intermediary
sections.body: Any person who on behalf of another receives, stores or transmits electronic records or provides related services — as defined; relevant to safe-harbour analysis under s. 79.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the term; quote the definition; apply to facts before invoking operative sections.

examples.title: Is a smartphone a computer resource?
examples.body: Under s. 2, computer resource is broadly defined to include computer systems and related data; device classification follows the statutory text, not everyday labels alone.

hypotheticals.question: Can s. 43 apply without checking s. 2 definitions?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Whether the target is a computer resource and whether the act is access or download depends on s. 2.

distinctions.title: s. 2 definitions vs operative duties
distinctions.left: Defines terms used in the Act.
distinctions.right: ss. 43, 65–67 create civil and criminal liability using those terms.

misconceptions.trap: s. 2 is only dictionary material and can be ignored.
misconceptions.correction: Operative civil and criminal sections are controlled by these definitions.
